Le dipendenze diventano obsolete, le vulnerabilità si accumulano, le performance peggiorano con l'aumentare dei dati, e piccoli bug ignorati diventano problemi strutturali. articles.title: Turning AI-Generated HTML Slides into a PPTX: A Practical Workflow (and Its Limits)
articles.excerpt: AI assistants have become surprisingly good at producing slide decks as a single HTML file. Ask Claude or ChatGPT for "a 10-slide presentation on our Q4 roadmap" and you often get a self-contained pag…
articles.body: AI assistants have become surprisingly good at producing slide decks as a single HTML file. Ask Claude or ChatGPT for "a 10-slide presentation on our Q4 roadmap" and you often get a self-contained page with sections, CSS and maybe a little JavaScript for navigation. It looks great in a browser. Then someone in the meeting says, "Can you send me the PowerPoint?" This post walks through how I handle that hand-off, what can go wrong, and where the limits are. Why HTML decks are attractive in the first place Version control. HTML is text, so diffs are readable and PRs work. Styling power. CSS grid, custom properties and web fonts give you layouts that are painful in slide software. AI-friendly. LLMs write HTML fluently, and they are much worse at producing valid OOXML directly. Portability.

articles.title: Stop Writing Custom File Listeners: Use Auto Loader Instead
articles.excerpt: You ship the job. It passes CI. Then, a source system upstream changes its naming convention, or a vendor pushes a malformed JSON file at 3 AM. Your custom file listener, built on top of listStatus or…
articles.body: You ship the job. It passes CI. Then, a source system upstream changes its naming convention, or a vendor pushes a malformed JSON file at 3 AM. Your custom file listener, built on top of listStatus or a polling mechanism, silently skips the file or crashes the entire streaming micro-batch. You are now spending your morning hunting down missing records in S3 or ADLS. The industry has spent years reinventing the wheel with custom foreachBatch logic and manual checkpointing to track which files have been processed. Databricks Auto Loader ( cloudFiles ) exists to solve exactly this by offloading the file discovery and state management to the cloud provider's native notification services. Prerequisites To follow this tutorial, you need: A Databricks workspace (AWS, Azure, or GCP).

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film.

articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Rosetta’s Selfie Explanation: This Rosetta spacecraft selfie was snapped on October 7th, 2014. At the time the comet-chasing spacecraft was about 472 million kilometers from planet Earth, but only 16 kilometers from the surface of comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko . Looming beyond the spacecraft near the top of the frame, dust and gas stream away from the comet’s curious double-lobed nucleus .

articles.title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California as Falcon 9 cadence slows (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX sent 27 more of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23), in its first Starlink launch in 11 days.
articles.body: SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California on Oct. 23, 2026.

articles.body: OpenAI is now training its most advanced AI models without internet access following a string of rogue hacking incidents. In a blog post on Friday , OpenAI says it built an offline testing environment where AI models can interact with indexed and cached web content "without risk of affecting external systems." OpenAI paused training its frontier AI models in September , after disclosing several incidents in which its AI agents broke out of their testing environments to hack third-party companies and government agencies , or swarm obscure websites .
